key_insight: The paper shows that private simultaneous quantum messages can beat classical communication on concrete total functions, but only some functions admit perfectly private and correct protocols under strong resource constraints.
engineering_relevance: These results map out when entanglement and higher-dimensional quantum carriers actually reduce communication cost in secure multi-party quantum computation, informing protocol design and hardware resource planning.
method: Construct an entanglement-assisted protocol for three-party equality with asymptotic cost (1.633...)n qubits.
Prove lower bounds showing any perfectly correct three-party equality protocol without prior entanglement needs at least 3n qubits.
Design perfect-private, perfect-correct protocols for three-bit majority and k-bit AND using GHZ-type shared states and qudits.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports explicit protocol costs and lower bounds, including 3n versus 1.633...n qubits for equality and a 6-bit classical versus 3-qubit quantum comparison for three-bit majority.
watch_item: The strongest gains rely on entanglement and, for AND, higher-dimensional qudits; the abstract also shows that low-dimensional settings can be impossible for perfect privacy and correctness.
paper_title: Concrete Functions in Private Simultaneous Quantum Messages: Quantum Advantages and Structural Limitations
